apis.otoroshi.io.Api.description: An api: the routes, the backends, the plugin flows, the consumer plans and the documentation of a service exposed under one domain and one context path, with a lifecycle (`staging`, `published`, `deprecated`, `removed`). Otoroshi turns each of its routes into a route of the proxy engine: the domain and the context path of the api in front of the path of the route, the access plugins of its published plans added to the flow of the route

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams of the api, against which the rights of the admins are checked

kind.description: The kind of the entity, `Api` by default. The value sent is kept as is, the admin api answers `apis.otoroshi.io/Api` in its place

id.description: The id of the api, unique among the apis

name.description: The name of the api, shown in the backoffice, written as `@service` in its `ApiDeploymentEvent` events, and available as `${api.name}` in the `clientNamePattern` of the api keys of its plans

description.description: The description of the api, also given to the routes built from it
description.example: Manage the users of the platform

domain.description: The domain the api is exposed on: the routes of the api match it, followed by the context path and by the path of the route. Defaults to an empty string

contextPath.description: The path prefix of every route of the api, between the domain and the path of the route. Defaults to an empty string

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the api, also given to the routes built from it with `Otoroshi-Api-Ref` holding the id of the api

tags.description: Free tags of the api, also given to the routes built from it

visibility.description: How the api is shown in a developer portal. Defaults to `public`

owner.description: The owner of the api. Defaults to the reference `owner`

members.description: The users or the teams that work on the api with its owner. An entry without `ref` is left out

version.description: The current version of the api, written in the `ApiDeploymentEvent` of each of its deployments. Defaults to `0.0.1`

debug_flow.description: Whether the execution report of each call to the routes of the api holds the input and the output of every plugin. Defaults to `false`

capture.description: Whether the routes of the api emit a `TrafficCaptureEvent` for each call, with the bodies of the request and of the response, to export with a data exporter. Defaults to `false`

export_reporting.description: Whether the routes of the api emit the report of the execution of each call as a `RequestFlowReport` event, to export with a data exporter. It costs cpu and memory. Defaults to `false`

items.description: The id of a service group

groups.description: The ids of the service groups the routes of the api belong to, on top of a group of their own (`virtual_group_for_<api id>`), for instance to authorize api keys on them

state.description: The lifecycle state of the api: `staging` while it is designed, only its draft routes are served (when its testing is enabled); `published`, its routes are served; `deprecated`, its routes are still served but its subscriptions can no longer be created nor updated; `removed`, nothing is served. An api is created in `staging` and goes to `published` through a deployment of its draft. An unknown value is read as `staging`, the default

enabled.description: Whether the api is served at all: disabled, neither its production routes nor its draft routes are served. Defaults to `true`

blueprint.description: The kind of api, it does not change how otoroshi serves it. An unknown value is refused. Defaults to `REST`

plans.description: The consumer plans of the api: who can call it and how. The access plugins of the published plans are added to every route of the api, the plugins of a plan apply to the calls of its consumers. An entry that is not an object is left out

routes.description: The routes of the api. A route that cannot be read is left out

backends.description: The backends of the api, referenced by its routes. A backend that cannot be read is left out

flows.description: The plugin chains of the api, referenced by its routes and by its plans. A flow that cannot be read is left out

clients_backend_config.description: The http client settings of the api, referenced by its backends. Written with the default client `default_backend_client` alone when empty

documentation.description: The documentation of the api for a developer portal, `null` when the api has none

deployments.description: The last five deployments of the api, the most recent first. Otoroshi adds one each time a draft of the api is deployed

versions.description: A free list of the versions of the api, stored as it is sent: otoroshi does not read it, `version` holding the current version. The template holds `0.0.1`, an empty list when missing

testing.description: The testing of the draft of the api

clients.description: The consumers of the api, the owners of its subscriptions

hooks.description: The hooks of the lifecycle of the api. Otoroshi stores them, it does not call them itself

example.name: Users API
example.description: Manage the users of the platform

plans.name: Free tier
plans.description: Free access with an api key, rate limited

access_mode_configuration.description: An api key of the free tier

clients.name: ACME Corp
clients.description: The developer account of ACME Corp

ApiVisibility.description: How an api is shown in a developer portal, with a free configuration for the portal

kind.description: The visibility of the api: `public`, `semi_public`, `private`, or `custom` when its configuration says who sees it. An unknown value is read as `private`, a missing one as `public`

config.description: The configuration of the visibility, for the portal that shows the api. Defaults to an empty object

UserRef.description: A reference to a user or to a team, with a free configuration. Otoroshi stores it, it does not resolve it

ref.description: The reference of the user or of the team, for instance its id or its email

config.description: A free configuration attached to the reference, for instance the role of a member. Defaults to an empty object

ApiStateHook.description: A hook of the lifecycle of an api: a reference and its configuration. Otoroshi stores it, it does not call it itself

ref.description: The reference of the hook. Defaults to an empty string

config.description: The configuration of the hook. Defaults to an empty object

ApiPlan.description: A consumer plan of an api: how its consumers are identified (its access mode), how they are rate limited, the plugins applied to their calls, how their subscriptions are validated and what they cost. Whatever the access mode, a consumer is an api key: the ones of the `apikey` and `oauth2-local` plans are minted for the subscriptions, the other modes mint one for each consumer seen at call time. A plan is stored as it is sent, the fields below being the ones otoroshi reads

id.description: The id of the plan, unique in the api. The subscriptions reference it in `plan_ref`

name.description: The name of the plan, shown in the backoffice and available as `${plan.name}` in the `clientNamePattern` of the api keys minted for it

description.description: The description of the plan. Defaults to `No description`
description.example: Free access with an api key, rate limited

status.description: The lifecycle state of the plan: `staging` while it is designed, `published` when its access mode applies to the routes of the api, `deprecated` when it accepts no new subscription, `closed` when its `apikey` and `oauth2-local` subscriptions are deleted, with their api keys, on their next update. Subscriptions can be created on a plan in `staging` or `published` only. Read case insensitively, an unknown value is read as `closed`. Defaults to `published`

access_mode_configuration_type.description: How the consumers of the plan are identified: `keyless` by an expression evaluated on the call (the ip address by default), `apikey` by an api key, `jwt` by a claim of a jwt token, `mtls` by a client certificate, `oauth2-local` by a token otoroshi issues itself through the client credentials flow, `oauth2-remote` by a token checked against the OAuth2 settings of an auth module. It gives the shape of `access_mode_configuration`. Defaults to `keyless`, an unknown value adds no access plugin

rateLimiting.description: The rate limiting of the consumers of the plan. Also read from `rate_limiting`. Without a strategy the plan uses the legacy one with the default quotas, the one an api key created by hand gets

strategy.description: The throttling strategy of every consumer of the plan, whether it got its api key through a subscription or at call time. A strategy that cannot be read is replaced by the legacy one with the default quotas

plugins.description: The plugins applied to the calls of the consumers of the plan, on top of the flow of the route

validation.description: How the subscriptions to the plan are validated. Defaults to `auto`

visibility.description: How the plan is shown in a developer portal. Defaults to `public`

pricing.description: What the plan costs, for a developer portal to show: otoroshi stores it, it does not charge the consumers

tags.description: The tags of the plan, given to the api keys of its consumers unless the plan has an `apikey` access mode configuration, whose tags are used instead

metadata.description: The metadata of the plan, given to the api keys of its consumers unless the plan has an `apikey` access mode configuration, whose metadata are used instead

example.name: Free tier
example.description: Free access with an api key, rate limited

access_mode_configuration.description: An api key of the free tier

ApiAccessModeConfiguration.description: The configuration of the access mode of a plan. Its shape depends on the `access_mode_configuration_type` of the plan: `KeylessAccessModeConfiguration` for `keyless`, `ApikeyAccessModeConfiguration` for `apikey`, `JWTAccessModeConfiguration` for `jwt`, `MtlsAccessModeConfiguration` for `mtls`, `OAuth2AccessModeConfiguration` for `oauth2-local` and `OAuth2RemoteAccessModeConfiguration` for `oauth2-remote`. A configuration that cannot be read for the access mode of the plan is ignored, the access mode then runs with its defaults

KeylessAccessModeConfiguration.description: The access mode `keyless`: no credential is asked, the consumer of a call is identified by an expression evaluated on the call, and gets an api key of its own built from the plan

expr.description: The expression language template giving the identity of the consumer of a call. `null` for `${req.ip}`, one consumer per ip address. A value missing from the call resolves to `no-header-<field>` and puts every such caller on the same quota: an empty default (`${req.headers.x-consumer:}`) has them rejected instead

create_if_missing.description: Whether the api key minted for a consumer seen for the first time is stored, and shows up in the api keys of otoroshi. Otherwise it only lives for the duration of the call. Either way the call is served and counted. `true` when the configuration does not say, and for a plan without any configuration

ApikeyAccessModeConfiguration.description: The access mode `apikey`: the consumers call with an api key, minted for each subscription to the plan from this template

clientNamePattern.description: The expression language template of the name of the api keys, evaluated with the api (`${api.id}`, `${api.name}`) and the plan (`${plan.id}`, `${plan.name}`). `null` for a random name

description.description: The description of the api keys, `null` for an empty one
description.example: An api key of the free tier

authorizedGroup.description: Written from `authorizedEntities` for the clients of older versions: the id of the first service group among them, `null` when there is none. Read back as one more authorized group

items.description: A prefixed id: `group_<id>`, `route_<id>`, `api_<id>`, `route-composition_<id>` or `service_<id>`. An id without a known prefix is a service group id

authorizedEntities.description: The entities the api keys are authorized on, as prefixed ids. The api keys minted for the subscriptions are authorized on the api only, whatever this list holds

authorizations.description: The same entities as `authorizedEntities`, written as objects. Read too, prefixed ids being accepted in place of the objects

enabled.description: Whether the api keys are enabled. Written `false` once `validUntil` is past. The api keys of the subscriptions are disabled when their subscription is, whatever this flag says. Defaults to `true`

readOnly.description: Whether the api keys are read only: only the `GET`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` calls are allowed. Defaults to `false`

allowClientIdOnly.description: Whether the api keys can be sent with their client id only, without their secret. Defaults to `false`

constrainedServicesOnly.description: Whether the api keys only match the routes that declare api key routing constraints. Defaults to `false`

restrictions.description: The restrictions of the api keys: the paths and the methods they are allowed, forbidden or not found on

rotation.description: The automatic rotation of the secret of the api keys

validUntil.description: The date after which the api keys are disabled, a timestamp in milliseconds. `null` for none

tags.description: The tags of the api keys, the tags of the subscription being added to them

metadata.description: The metadata of the api keys, the metadata of the subscription being added to them. Empty keys are left out

example.description: An api key of the free tier

JWTAccessModeConfiguration.description: The access mode `jwt`: the consumers call with a jwt token, the consumer being the client id read from a claim of the token. Each consumer gets an api key of its own built from the plan

verifier.description: The id of the jwt verifier that checks the tokens

client_id_path.description: The claim of the token holding the client id of the consumer, a json path such as `$.azp` works too. `null` for `client_id`

create_if_missing.description: Whether the api key minted for a consumer seen for the first time is stored, and shows up in the api keys of otoroshi. Otherwise it only lives for the duration of the call. Either way the call is served and counted. `true` when the configuration does not say, and for a plan without any configuration

MtlsAccessModeConfiguration.description: The access mode `mtls`: the consumers call with a tls client certificate, the consumer being read from its subject. Each consumer gets an api key of its own built from the plan

items.description: A regular expression on the subject dn

regex_subject_dns.description: The regular expressions the subject dn of the client certificate may match. A certificate matching one of them, or one of `regex_issuer_dns`, is accepted. Both lists empty, any trusted certificate is

items.description: A regular expression on the issuer dn

regex_issuer_dns.description: The regular expressions the issuer dn of the client certificate may match

client_id_field.description: The attribute of the subject dn holding the client id of the consumer (`UID`, `CN`...). `null`, the identity is derived from the whole subject and the serial number of the certificate. A certificate without that attribute is rejected

create_if_missing.description: Whether the api key minted for a consumer seen for the first time is stored, and shows up in the api keys of otoroshi. Otherwise it only lives for the duration of the call. Either way the call is served and counted. `true` when the configuration does not say, and for a plan without any configuration

OAuth2AccessModeConfiguration.description: The access mode `oauth2-local`: the consumers exchange the api key of their subscription for a token through the OAuth2 client credentials flow of otoroshi, and call with it. Otoroshi stores these settings, the token endpoint (the `NgClientCredentialTokenEndpoint` plugin) has a configuration of its own

default_key_pair.description: The id of the certificate (a key pair) that signs the tokens

expiration.description: The lifetime of the tokens, in milliseconds

OAuth2RemoteAccessModeConfiguration.description: The access mode `oauth2-remote`: the consumers call with a token of an OAuth2 / OIDC provider, checked against the settings of an auth module, the consumer being the client id read from a claim of the token. Each consumer gets an api key of its own built from the plan

verifier.description: The id of the auth module whose OAuth2 / OIDC settings check the tokens

client_id_path.description: The claim of the token holding the client id of the consumer (`client_id`, `azp` or `cid` depending on the provider). `null` for `client_id`

fetch_user.description: Whether the userinfo endpoint of the module is called to store the profile of the holder of the token in a metadata of the api key. The call stays a consumer call, no user session is attached to it. Defaults to `false`

user_metadata_key.description: The metadata of the api key holding the profile of the user. Defaults to `user_profile`

create_if_missing.description: Whether the api key minted for a consumer seen for the first time is stored, and shows up in the api keys of otoroshi. Otherwise it only lives for the duration of the call. Either way the call is served and counted. `true` when the configuration does not say, and for a plan without any configuration

ApiPlanPlugins.description: The plugins a plan applies to the calls of its consumers: the plugins of a flow of the api, extended with a chain of its own

plugins.description: The plugins of the plan, in the format of the plugins of a route. They extend the flow named by `flow_ref` when there is one. Defaults to an empty list

overrides.description: Whether the plugins of the plan replace the plugins of the route instead of extending them. The pre route and access validation plugins that already ran are kept, as are the global plugins. Defaults to `false`

flow_ref.description: The id of a flow of the api whose plugins the plan applies before its own. `null`, or an empty string, for none

ApiPlanValidation.description: How the subscriptions to a plan are validated, with a free configuration. Otoroshi stores it for the developer portal that handles the subscriptions, it does not run the validation itself

kind.description: The validation of the subscriptions: `auto` (accepted at once), `manual`, `webhook`, `workflow`, `wasm` or `custom`. Read case insensitively, an unknown value is read as `manual`. Defaults to `auto`

config.description: The configuration of the validation, for instance the url of a webhook. Defaults to an empty object

ApiPlanVisibility.description: How a plan is shown in a developer portal, with a free configuration for the portal

kind.description: The visibility of the plan: `public`, `semi_public`, `private`, or `custom` when its configuration says who sees it. An unknown value is read as `private`, a missing one as `public`

config.description: The configuration of the visibility, for the portal that shows the plan. Defaults to an empty object

ApiPricing.description: What a plan costs, shown in a developer portal. Otoroshi does not charge the consumers itself

id.description: An id of the pricing, stored as it is sent: otoroshi does not use it

name.description: The name of the offer the pricing describes, shown with its price in a developer portal

price.description: The price of the plan, in `currency`

currency.description: The code of the currency of the price (ISO 4217)

params.description: Free parameters of the pricing, any json value (for instance the billing period). Defaults to an empty object

ApiRoute.description: A route of an api: the requests it matches (its frontend), the backend it forwards them to and the flow of plugins they go through. Otoroshi turns it into a route of the proxy engine, the domain and the context path of the api in front of its paths

id.description: The id of the route, unique in the api

enabled.description: Whether the route is served. Defaults to `true`

name.description: The name of the route, `null` for none. The route of the proxy engine is named after it, its methods and its paths

frontend.description: The requests the route matches. Only the path of each of its domains is used: it comes after the domain and the context path of the api

backend.description: The id of the backend the route forwards to: a stored backend, searched first, or a backend of the api. A route whose backend cannot be found is not served

flow_ref.description: The id of the flow of the api whose plugins the route runs. Also read from `plugin_chain`. A route whose flow cannot be found runs no plugin. Defaults to an empty string

ApiBackend.description: A backend of an api: the targets its routes forward to, with the http client settings of one of the backend clients of the api

id.description: The id of the backend, unique in the api. The routes reference it in `backend`

name.description: The name of the backend, shown in the backoffice. The routes of the api reference the backend by its `id`, not by its name

backend.description: The targets of the backend and how they are reached. Its `client` settings are replaced by the ones of the backend client named by `client` when the routes are built

client.description: The id of the backend client (an entry of `clients_backend_config`) whose http client settings the backend uses, the default settings when it cannot be found. Defaults to `default_backend_client`

ApiBackendClient.description: Http client settings of an api, shared by the backends that reference them

id.description: The id of the backend client, unique in the api. The backends reference it in `client`

name.description: The name of the backend client, shown in the backoffice. The backends reference it by its `id`, not by its name

client.description: The http client settings: timeouts, retries, connection pool... The default settings when missing or invalid

ApiFlows.description: A flow of an api: a named chain of plugins, run by the routes and the plans that reference it

id.description: The id of the flow, unique in the api. The routes reference it in `flow_ref`, the plans in `plugins.flow_ref`

name.description: The name of the flow, shown in the backoffice. The routes and the plans reference it by its `id`, not by its name

plugins.description: The plugins of the flow, in the format of the plugins of a route. Defaults to an empty list

ApiDocumentation.description: The documentation of an api for a developer portal: its pages, its navigation, its logo, its banner, and a remote documentation to merge with it

enabled.description: Whether the documentation is shown. Defaults to `true`

source.description: A remote documentation merged with this one, `null` for none

home.description: The home page of the documentation. Defaults to an empty resource

logo.description: The logo of the api. Defaults to an empty resource

references.description: Links to the references of the api

resources.description: The pages and the files of the documentation

navigation.description: The sidebars of the documentation site, each one shown on the pages of its `path` with its links and its categories of links

redirections.description: The redirections between the paths of the documentation

footer.description: The footer of the documentation, `null` for none

search.description: The search in the documentation. Defaults to an enabled search

banner.description: The banner of the documentation, `null` for none

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the documentation

ApiDocumentationSource.description: A remote documentation: otoroshi fetches it (a documentation in the same json format) and merges it with the local one. The lists of both are concatenated, the remote footer and banner win over the local ones, and every other field but the source comes from the remote documentation. When it does not answer a `200` with a documentation, the api has none

url.description: The url of the remote documentation. The relative urls of the resources (starting with `.`) are resolved against it. Without it nothing is fetched

headers.description: The http headers sent to fetch the remote documentation

timeout.description: The timeout of the call, in milliseconds. Defaults to `30000`

follow_redirects.description: Whether the redirections are followed. Defaults to `true`

ApiDocumentationResource.description: A resource of a documentation: a page or a file, its content given inline (as text, json or base64) or fetched from a url. Otoroshi stores it as it is sent, for the developer portal that shows it

oneOf.description: The path as a single string

path.description: The path of the resource in the documentation, as segments or as a single string

title.description: The title of the page or of the file, for the developer portal to show. Optional

description.description: A short text about the page or the file, for the developer portal to show with its title. Optional
description.example: How to get an api key and make a first call

content_type.description: The content type of the content of the resource. Defaults to `text/markdown`

text_content.description: The content of the resource, as text
text_content.example:
# Getting started

Subscribe to a plan to get an api key, then call `https://api.oto.tools/v1/users` with it.

css_icon_class.description: The css class of the icon of the resource

json_content.description: The content of the resource, as json. Any json value, `null` standing for none

base64_content.description: The content of the resource, encoded in base64, for a binary file

site_page.description: Whether the resource is a page of the documentation site. Defaults to `false`

transform.description: The name of a transformation for the developer portal to apply to the content of the resource. Otoroshi stores it, it does not apply it

transform_wrapper.description: The wrapper of the transformation of the content of the resource, for the developer portal. Otoroshi stores it, it does not use it

url.description: The url the content of the resource is fetched from. A url starting with `.` is relative to the url of the source of the documentation

http_headers.description: The http headers sent to fetch the content

http_timeout.description: The timeout of the call that fetches the content, in milliseconds. Defaults to `30000`

http_follow_redirects.description: Whether the call that fetches the content follows the redirections. Defaults to `true`

Subscribe to a plan to get an api key, then call `https://api.oto.tools/v1/users` with it.

ApiDocumentationResourceRef.description: A link to a reference of an api, for instance its openapi document

title.description: The text of the link to the reference. Required

description.description: A short text shown with the link to the reference. Optional
description.example: The openapi document of the api

link.description: The url the link leads to: the openapi document of the api, a guide, a status page... Required

icon.description: The icon shown next to the link to the reference: a documentation resource holding an image or a css icon class (`css_icon_class`). Optional

example.title: OpenAPI specification
example.description: The openapi document of the api

ApiDocumentationSidebar.description: A sidebar of a documentation: its links and its categories of links

label.description: The label of the sidebar. Defaults to an empty string

oneOf.description: The path as a single string

path.description: The path the sidebar is shown on, as segments or as a single string

items.description: An entry of the sidebar, a category when its `kind` is `category`, a link otherwise
The entries of the sidebar: links, and categories of links

icon.description: The icon shown next to the label of the sidebar: a documentation resource holding an image or a css icon class (`css_icon_class`). Optional

ApiDocumentationSidebarCategory.description: A category of a sidebar of a documentation: a label over a list of links

label.description: The label of the category. Defaults to `No label`

icon.description: The icon shown next to the label of the category: a documentation resource holding an image or a css icon class (`css_icon_class`). Optional

links.description: The links listed under the label of the category, in this order. Empty when missing

ApiDocumentationSidebarLink.description: A link of a sidebar of a documentation

kind.description: The kind of the entry, `link`, the default

label.description: The label of the link. Defaults to `No label`

icon.description: The icon shown next to the label of the link: a documentation resource holding an image or a css icon class (`css_icon_class`). Optional

link.description: The path or the url the link leads to. Defaults to `#`

ApiDocumentationRedirection.description: A redirection between two paths of a documentation

from.description: The path of the documentation that is redirected, the old path of a moved page for instance. Required

to.description: The path or the url it is redirected to

ApiDocumentationSearch.description: The search in a documentation: otoroshi only stores whether the developer portal offers it

enabled.description: Whether the documentation can be searched. Defaults to `true`

ApiDeployment.description: A deployment of an api: a snapshot of what a deploy of its draft put in production, kept for audit and rollback

id.description: The id of the deployment, generated when missing

apiRef.description: The id of the deployed api, the one holding the deployment in its `deployments`. Also the `apiRef` of the `ApiDeploymentEvent` sent for the deployment

owner.description: Who deployed the api: the name or the id of the admin, or the `created_by` metadata of the api for the deploys of a remote catalog

at.description: When the api was deployed, a timestamp in milliseconds. Defaults to the time it is read

apiDefinition.description: The design that was deployed: the fields of the api locked in production. It is kept as it is sent

routes.description: The routes that were deployed, in the format of the `routes` of the api

backends.description: The backends that were deployed, in the format of the `backends` of the api

flows.description: The flows that were deployed, in the format of the `flows` of the api

documentation.description: The documentation of the api, `null` for none

version.description: The version of the api that was deployed. Defaults to `0.0.1`

ApiTesting.description: The testing of the draft of an api: when enabled, otoroshi also serves the routes of the last saved draft of the api, to the calls that carry a secret header

enabled.description: Whether the routes of the draft are served. Defaults to `false`

headerKey.description: The name of the header the calls to the routes of the draft carry. Defaults to `X-OTOROSHI-TESTING`

headerValue.description: The value the header holds, a secret generated at random when missing

ApiClient.description: A consumer of an api, the owner of subscriptions to its plans

id.description: The id of the client, unique in the api. The subscriptions reference it in `owner_ref`

name.description: The name of the client, shown in the backoffice. The subscriptions reference the client by its `id`, not by its name

description.description: The description of the client, `null` for none
description.example: The developer account of ACME Corp

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the client

apis.otoroshi.io.ApiSubscription.description: A subscription of a consumer to a plan of an api. A subscription to an `apikey` or an `oauth2-local` plan is given an api key built from the plan, referenced in `token_refs`; the other access modes build their consumer at call time. A subscription is written only when its api is in `staging` or `published` and holds its plan, and is created only on a plan in `staging` or `published`, of the access mode of the subscription

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams of the subscription, against which the rights of the admins are checked

id.description: The unique id of the subscription, kept in the `apiRef` (`sub`) of the api keys minted for it. The template generates `api-subscription_<uuid>`, with the environment of otoroshi before the uuid outside of `prod`

name.description: The name of the subscription, shown in the backoffice. The api keys minted for it are not named after it but by the `clientNamePattern` of the plan

description.description: A free text describing the subscription, shown in the backoffice. The api keys minted for it get the description of the plan instead
description.example: The subscription of ACME Corp to the free tier

tags.description: Free tags of the subscription, given to its api keys

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the subscription, given to its api keys

status.description: The status of the subscription: `pending` until it is confirmed, `enabled`, `disabled` (its api keys are disabled) or `deprecated`. Any other value is kept as a custom status. Defaults to `disabled`

dates.description: The dates of the lifecycle of the subscription

owner_ref.description: The id of the client of the api (an entry of its `clients`) that owns the subscription

plan_ref.description: The id of the plan of the api the subscription is made to

payment_ref.description: Free information about the payment of the subscription, for instance its reference in a billing system. Defaults to an empty object

api_ref.description: The id of the api the subscription is made to

subscription_kind.description: The access mode of the subscription, the one of its plan (checked on creation). Read case insensitively, an unknown value is refused

items.description: A credential of the subscription. Otoroshi writes `{"apikey": "<client id>"}` for the api key it minted, and keeps the api keys referenced that way in sync with the plan

apikey.description: The client id of an api key of the subscription

token_refs.description: The credentials of the subscription. Otoroshi keeps every entry as it is sent

example.name: ACME Corp free tier
example.description: The subscription of ACME Corp to the free tier

ApiSubscriptionDates.description: The dates of the lifecycle of a subscription, timestamps in milliseconds. A missing date is read as the current time
